claim: QST-SIM-0002 now has an accepted finite-time stale-coverage measurement primitive and an accepted two-constant-rotation-regime measurement under one identical body-fixed observation schedule, with equal traces and no demonstrated policy advantage.

provenance.source_title: Measure stale coverage under two constant rotation regimes
limitations: Identical body-fixed observations yielded equal stale-coverage traces and do not establish a policy or architecture advantage.
Irregular or tumbling rotation, alternative observation geometry, and new shadow physics remain outside scope.
provenance.fact_summary: The accepted artifact records stale-coverage fractions [0.5, 1.0] for both 2-hour and 12-hour constant-rotation regimes under the same synthetic observation schedule.
provenance.negative_lineage: The August 12 candidate failed semantic validation before the finite-time repair, and the August 14 candidate later exposed a malformed governance receipt before revalidation and merge. Both failures remain preserved in accepted receipts.
provenance.inference_summary: SNS has a stronger policy-neutral measurement boundary, while the current observation schedule is not informative about rotation-regime effects.
provenance.speculation_summary: A future observation geometry that couples observations to rotation may reveal a regime effect without embedding a survey-policy preference.
